runConfig.positivePrompt: Static locked wide camera, one continuous five-second shot with no cuts. Preserve the attached approved still as the exact first-frame anatomy, identity, composition, lighting, palette, and background reference. Exactly one complete full-body Tyrannosaurus rex stands firmly in place. The torso, pelvis, hips, two planted hind feet and toes, two tiny chest-held forelimbs with exactly two fingers on each readable hand, and complete heavy tail remain motionless at their source coordinates. Only the continuously attached deep head, short muscular neck, throat, and lower jaw move. During the first second the mouth remains closed. Then the head lifts only slightly while the lower jaw opens smoothly in one direction from closed to a natural twenty-five-degree gape. The upper skull does not bend or move toward the frame edge. Stable upper and lower tooth rows, one low tongue, and the dark mouth interior become visible. The throat expands once. During the final second hold the open-mouth silent display. Do not close the jaw, return, recoil, nod repeatedly, reverse, or loop. Preserve the broad posterior skull, narrowing snout, low rounded postorbital bosses, small polygonal scales, uninterrupted neck attachment, and all locked body parts. Silent, non-graphic generated behavior hypothesis for ages five to fourteen.
